question: Should typed transient tool progress become a supported shared reply contract, and must Slack continue honoring `streaming.preview.toolProgress: false` as separate message delivery?
rationale: The current patch creates a permanent cross-plugin behavior contract and changes a documented user preference; neither API ownership nor the compatibility policy can be safely inferred from implementation alone.

options.title: Typed intent with policy gating
options.body: Add a typed shared transient-progress intent and let Slack's resolved streaming settings select preview, reaction, separate delivery, or suppression.

options.title: Redefine Slack progress behavior
options.body: Intentionally make marked Codex progress never post as standalone Slack messages, then update documentation and provide explicit upgrade proof for that compatibility change.

options.title: Move suppression upstream
options.body: Pause this channel-specific patch and handle transient progress centrally in the shared streaming/reply owner used by all channel plugins.

recommendation.title: Typed intent with policy gating
recommendation.body: Add a typed shared transient-progress intent and let Slack's resolved streaming settings select preview, reaction, separate delivery, or suppression.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans the Slack delivery and thread behavior where the documented preference and message-delivery compatibility decision lands.
